articles.title: Analysis-Investors press Amazon, Microsoft and Google on water, power use in US data centers
articles.mainIdea: Analysis-Investors press Amazon, Microsoft and Google on water, power use in US data centers
articles.summary: Reuters: Analysis-Investors press Amazon, Microsoft and Google on water, power use in US data centers. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet's Google have each recently abandoned construction of multibillion-dollar data centers over community opposition and now the companies are coming under shareholder pressure over the environmental impact of their projects. More ‌than a dozen investors are cranking up the heat on companies ahead of annual shareholder meetings this spring, seeking more data on the ‌tech giants' water usage and conservation efforts as they seek to expand their computing power, according to interviews with Reuters. Trillium Asset Management, a Boston-based firm with more than $4 billion in assets under ​management, filed a resolution with Alphabet in December seeking clarity on how it will meet existing climate goals given the surging energy needs of its data centers, Andrea Ranger, director of shareholder advocacy, said in an interview. Related tickers mentioned: AMZN, GOOG, MSFT.

articles.title: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?
articles.mainIdea: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal: Do Companies That Stack the Vote Do Worse?. Allbirds wasn’t just the unofficial footwear provider of Silicon Valley—its initial public offering in 2021 tapped into the tech sector’s ethos by giving the company’s founders disproportionate sway in how it would be run. Salad chain Sweetgreen eyewear seller Warby Parker language-learning app Duolingo and social network Snap all have share classes with extra votes for founders and each has incinerated billions in shareholder wealth recently. The structure had a revival last year with companies like Klarna, Figma and StubHub. Related tickers mentioned: BIRD, BRK-B, CMCSA, DDS, META, WRBY.
